contactCornerLines: whism of whiff with a touch of whimsy

projects.title: Unity Compute Shader Raytracing Lab
projects.description: I built this as my little photon playground: compute threads per pixel, camera rays, sphere hits, GPU buffers, and materials that make math glow.
projects.story: I wanted the screen to feel like a lab bench where light leaves fingerprints.
projects.imageAlt: Raytracing lab render from the project repository

projects.title: Meantendo
projects.description: I packed a tiny arcade creature into an ESP32: joystick, buttons, buzzer, ST7735 display, menus, and games that feel too stubborn to stay on breadboard wires.
projects.story: I wanted a pocket console that looked like it escaped from a weekend workshop.
projects.imageAlt: Meantendo handheld console preview from the repository

projects.title: ShadowIntern
projects.description: I made a fake workstation that remembers your grind, pokes at burnout, hands out XP, mutters through procedural audio, and slowly turns work into a tiny universe.
projects.story: I wanted the UI to feel like it was quietly judging my productivity from inside a CRT.

projects.title: C-L-I-T
projects.description: I rebuilt the bones of Git in C, from init and SHA-1 objects to index, trees, commits, logs, and checkout, because black boxes annoy me.
projects.story: I took Git apart like a strange mechanical watch and tried to make it tick again.

projects.title: Smart Agriculture Disease Detection
projects.description: I wired an ESP32-CAM to a Flask brain so plants can get photographed, diagnosed, and sprayed by a tiny machine that thinks it is a farm medic.
projects.story: I wanted code to leave the screen and actually move water in the real world.

projects.title: NovelPedia Production Surfaces
projects.description: I work on production Next.js, React, Django, and PostgreSQL surfaces where reader flows, dashboards, uploads, banners, and tiny UX frictions all need to behave.
projects.story: I like the unglamorous fixes because that is where a product stops feeling like a mockup and starts feeling alive.

chapters.title: Builder before job title
chapters.body: I am Ankit Chetri, also Debyte, and I keep building things that leak between software and objects: web apps, bots, hardware toys, shader experiments, and tiny systems that teach me back.

chapters.title: Sebastian Lague Legacy
chapters.body: I love the Sebastian Lague kind of curiosity: explain the machine, visualize the invisible, make the hard thing playful, then ship the weird prototype before doubt catches up.

chapters.title: Cinema, anime, cats, food, sawdust
chapters.body: I want this place to feel like my desk after midnight: anime poster energy, sawdust, baking notes, shader tabs, cat interruptions, and cinematography sneaking into the way I frame code.

experience.body: I shipped 21+ merged PRs across production reader, author-dashboard, and admin-panel surfaces, the kind of work where polish and patience both matter.
experience.certificateNote: Official work proof not added yet.

experience.body: I built responsive author-dashboard interfaces with Next.js, TailwindCSS, Django REST APIs, and a lot of practical debugging under real product pressure.
I developed MongoDB-backed MERN and Flask modules for auth, payment, email workflows, third-party services, and APIs that had to connect cleanly.
